summary: Restaking is now one product among several at Solayer. The Solayer docs index lists Solayer Chain, sSOL, sUSD, Solayer Pay and sBridge sections, and DefiLlama groups Solayer, Solayer Restaking, Solayer USD and Solayer Card under one parent. DefiLlama's description still calls Solayer 'the restaking protocol on Solana', while the current Solayer docs call sSOL a liquid staking token. (from docs.solayer.org)

facts.text: One address, 5eosrve6LktMZgVNszYzebgmmC7BjLK8NoWyRQtcmGTF, is the upgrade authority of both Jito programs (read with mainnet JSON-RPC getAccountInfo on 2026-11-06). The Restaking Program was last deployed 2025-01-27 16:30 UTC. That matches JIP-6's note that the Jito DAO Security Council started upgrade votes on 2025-01-25 after a Certora audit. The Vault Program was last deployed 2025-04-17 01:11 UTC. The authority is a system-owned account, which fits a multisig vault and also a plain keypair. Which one it is was not checked.

Solayer's current docs describe sSOL as a liquid staking token and a 'universal liquidity layer', not as a restaking receipt. A user converts SOL or an LST to sSOL, and the pool stakes with Solayer's own validator ('Mega Validator'). A holder can then delegate sSOL to an endoAVS, which mints a wrapper token as proof of stake. An endoAVS is a Solana dApp that gains a higher chance of block space and transaction inclusion through stake-weighted quality of service (swQoS). The docs say 'each unit of sSOL represents a unit of blockspace'. Letting dApps pick the validators is described as future wo

Solayer's docs claim that stakers using its validator pay 0% commission and receive 100% of MEV, and they quote '10+% APY historical returns' for the sSOL pool. The docs describe the validator as a dedicated-hardware node in Ashburn, Virginia. These are vendor statements, and the sources read contain no independent check.

Solayer's restaking is now one product line among several. Its docs index groups content under Solayer Chain (InfiniSVM), sSOL, sUSD, Solayer Pay and LAYER staking, with no page titled restaking or slashing, and DefiLlama lists the Solayer parent with Solayer Restaking, Solayer USD and Solayer Card as separate protocols.

Solayer's drop was abrupt and Jito's gradual. Solayer lost 60% of TVL in 18 days ($352.6M on 2025-02-11 to $141.1M on 2025-03-01, with SOL held falling from 1.40M to 0.74M); 2025-02-11 is also the date of Binance Research's LAYER report, which gives listing-time token figures. Jito Restaking fell from $395.9M on 2025-07-01 to $198.8M on 2025-08-01 and $54.0M by 2025-12-01. No source read attributes either fall to a cause.

Jito (Re)staking is two upgradeable onchain programs. The Restaking Program (RestkWeAVL8fRGgzhfeoqFhsqKRchg6aa1XrcH96z4Q) is a registry of NCNs (node consensus networks) and operators. The Vault Program (Vau1t6sLNxnzB7ZDsef8TLbPLfyZMYXH8WTNqUdm9g8) holds staked SPL tokens, delegates them to approved operators and mints vault receipt tokens (VRTs). Immunefi's 2024 audit competition scoped exactly four assets: Restaking Core, Restaking Program, Vault Core and Vault Program.

Every connection in Jito (Re)staking needs mutual consent. NCNs, operators and vaults register separately, each side then opts in to the other, and a warm-up instruction activates the link (docs: one full epoch, not counting the current partial epoch). The SDK encodes this as ticket accounts with initialize, warmup and cooldown instructions for vault-NCN, operator-vault and slasher pairings, so no party can be connected unilaterally.

Jito (Re)staking is two onchain programs: the Restaking Program (RestkWeAVL8fRGgzhfeoqFhsqKRchg6aa1XrcH96z4Q), a registry of NCNs (node consensus networks) and operators, and the Vault Program (Vau1t6sLNxnzB7ZDsef8TLbPLfyZMYXH8WTNqUdm9g8), which holds deposited SPL tokens, delegates them to approved operators and mints vault receipt tokens (VRTs). Only coordination (delegation, votes, rewards, penalties) is tracked onchain; the NCN's real work runs offchain. The repo describes it as a framework for staking, restaking and liquid restaking on Solana and SVM environments.

Every Jito connection between an NCN, an operator and a vault is a pair of tickets that each warm up and cool down. The restaking_sdk instruction set has initialize, warm-up and cool-down instructions for NCN-vault, NCN-operator, operator-NCN and operator-vault links. The vault_sdk mirrors the NCN and slasher links. The docs say no party is connected automatically and that a warm-up lasts one full epoch, not counting the current partial epoch.

A Jito vault withdrawal ticket unlocks only when the current epoch is greater than the unstake epoch plus one (is_withdrawable in vault_staker_withdrawal_ticket.rs). The wait is therefore more than one full epoch and at most two. This reconciles the core-concepts page ('one full NCN-defined epoch') with the withdrawal guide ('two-epoch cooldown, about 4-5 days'): the guide states the worst case. The code takes epoch_length from the vault Config, whose default is Solana's DEFAULT_SLOTS_PER_EPOCH (432,000 slots). The live onchain value was not read.

At the Immunefi competition Jito listed three known issues that were not eligible for rewards: share-rate inflation by donating assets directly to a vault (mitigation: mint a small share amount at vault init, PR #150); fee changes between withdrawal-ticket enqueue and burn (fix still in progress); and an oversized cooldown reserve when a vault update epoch is missed or close_vault_update_state_tracker is not called (PR #163). Whether these were later merged was not verified.

A Jito vault needs a permissionless update cycle every epoch: InitializeVaultUpdateStateTracker, CrankVaultUpdateStateTracker, then CloseVaultUpdateStateTracker. Missed cranks caused real bugs. Jito's Immunefi known-issue list says the cooldown reserve can be too large if a vault update epoch is missed or close_vault_update_state_tracker is not called (PR 163). Certora finding H-02 says assets can skip a required cooldown when cranks are incomplete (fixed in PR 163). The repo added a cranker container image on 2025-09-26.

Connections are opt-in on every side. Operators and vaults register, then opt into an NCN; the NCN approves them and a warm-up instruction activates the link, so no party is connected automatically. A vault receipt token (VRT) can only be whitelisted for an NCN by three-way agreement among NCN developers, VRT providers and node operators, and third parties manage each NCN's allowlist.

Jito has no slashing execution path as of 2026-11-06. PR 141 ('VAULT: Remove Slash', merged 2024-10-24) deleted the vault Slash instruction and said 'Slash should be designed around that new information'. The current vault_sdk and restaking_sdk instruction enums still hold slasher opt-in tickets (for example InitializeNcnVaultSlasherTicket with max_slashable_per_epoch) but have no Slash variant. The docs (last updated 2025-08-13) say the slashing program 'is not currently live'. JIP-6 puts slashing in a third phase that needs approval from NCNs, node operators and VRT holders.

Skeptics argued before launch that Solana needs restaking less than Ethereum does. CoinDesk (updated 2024-05-01) quoted Multicoin's Tushar Jain ('Something that literally no developer has come to us and said is, "You know why users aren't using my product?"') and Blockworks Research's Ryan Connor ('just far less of a need than Ethereum'). A Blockworks Lightspeed piece, known only from a search-result summary because the page returned 403, quotes Fragmetric's Sang: 'Many people in the Solana ecosystem hate restaking.' The 2025-2026 TVL fall fits these views but no source ties them together.

The most serious audit findings cluster in withdrawal and per-epoch vault-update logic. OtterSec: burn-instruction bypass (Critical, PR #137), withdrawal-ticket desynchronisation DoS (PR #140), an unfair min_amount_out plus a skippable CrankVaultUpdateStateTracker call (PR #142 and #138), and over-withdrawing if a crank does not finish within an epoch. Certora H-02: assets over-unstaked when an update crank is incomplete (PR #163, merged 2024-12-23). Offside: CooldownVaultNcnTicket PDA validation always failed (fixed). Each vault must be cranked every epoch, and the crank steps can be called b

No public audit covers the code Jito has deployed or merged since 2024. The README audit table ends with Certora on 2024-12-23, yet the Vault Program was redeployed on 2025-04-17. The master branch has since gained SetConfigSecondaryAdmin (2025-08-07) and a PR titled 'AUDIT: 36675 - Add Revoke Token Delegation' (2025-08-11), and a PR adding Certora formal-verification rules has been open since 2025-08-06. The repo's security_audits folder holds only four 2024 PDFs. The Jito docs (last updated 2025-08-13) still say the programs are 'fully audited'.

Jito restaking has no executable slashing. In PR #141 (merged 2024-10-24) Jito removed the vault slash instruction, saying it chose removal over a no-op because 'Slash should be designed around that new information', and OtterSec's remediation for OS-JRS-ADV-01 was 'Remove the slashing instruction'. On master (read 2026-11-06) the vault and restaking SDK instruction lists hold slasher opt-in tickets and a SlasherAdmin role but no instruction that performs a slash, and the docs (updated 2025-08-13) say 'The slashing program is not currently live'.

Jito vaults do not support Token-2022. Offside Labs found (low, acknowledged) that a vault created with a Token-2022 mint is unusable, because the associated-token-account checks accept only the classic SPL Token program. Jito answered Certora's M-02 with 'Token2022 is no longer supported', and the finding is marked 'Confirmed, will not be fixed'. Issue 76 (opened 2024-08-26) and PR 271 (opened 2026-03-02, a byte-compatible subset only) remain open. The Immunefi competition page from November 2024 still says both programs support SPL Token and Token-2022.

Four audit reports sit in the repo's security_audits folder. OtterSec (assessed 2024-09-20 to 10-10, commit f04242f): 8 findings, 1 Critical (the burn instruction bypassed withdrawal-ticket checks), 4 High, 3 Info, all resolved. Certora report 1 (2024-08-08 to 09-19): 22 findings, 4 High, 7 Medium, 6 Low, 5 Info, 18 fixed. Certora report 2 (2024-10-31 to 11-11): 7 findings, 2 High, 3 Medium, 2 Low, 6 fixed. Offside Labs (2024-10-28 to 11-06): 1 Medium, 1 Low, 4 Info. That is 43 findings across the four reports, with 1 Critical and 10 High.

Jito (Re)staking is built from two onchain programs: the Restaking Program is a registry of NCNs (node consensus networks) and operators, and the Vault Program holds staked SPL tokens, delegates them to approved operators and issues vault receipt tokens (VRTs). The repo ships these as restaking_program and vault_program crates, with TypeScript SDKs.
Unstaking sSOL waits for a cooldown that 'typically lasts until the next Solana epoch (up to 2 days)'. The page mentions no instant-unstake route and no Solayer fee.
The Solayer delegation docs fetched do not mention slashing at all, so slashing conditions for sSOL delegated to an endoAVS were not found in the official pages read.

Jito's restaking repo (Apache-2.0, default branch master) ships the Rust programs, TypeScript SDKs (@jito-foundation/restaking-sdk and vault-sdk), a CLI and a vault cranker. GitHub lists five releases (v0.0.1 on 2024-09-04 to v1.0.0-cli on 2025-05-01), a last push on 2026-08-11, and only five commits (CLI, cranker, 'Vault Parity' keeper fixes) from 2026-07-24 to 2026-08-11 after a gap since 2026-02-24. The docs list program version 0.0.5.

Both TVL figures are mostly re-used staked SOL. About 91% of Jito Restaking's $14.8M is JitoSOL ($13.5M; 93% at the 2025-07-01 peak), and DefiLlama excludes JitoSOL from the Jito parent total to avoid double counting with liquid staking. Other vault tokens include JTO ($1.1M), KYROS, PIPE and NOMU. About 76% of Solayer's $9.76M is SOL ($7.41M), with $0.70M USDC and the rest LSTs; at its peak SOL was 83% and $31.6M was T-bills.

Leaving a vault uses a non-cancellable cooldown. The withdrawal guide (updated 2025-08-04) says two epochs, about 4-5 days, with rewards stopping at once, the VRT locked, a 0.1% withdrawal fee plus a 0.1% program fee (0.2% total) and possible extra vault fees. Selling the VRT on a secondary market avoids the wait but may trade at a premium or discount. The JitoSOL overview (2025-08-13) repeats two epochs and 'Your funds remain locked during this period'.

TipRouter is the only Jito NCN with disclosed usage and revenue. The Jito docs call it the 'flagship' NCN. Blockworks' Q2 2026 report says it collects tips and, since JIP-16, priority fees and distributes them to stakers for a 3% fee, split 2.7% to the DAO treasury, 0.15% to JitoSOL stakers and 0.15% to JTO stakers. The same report names no other NCN and does not mention VRT vaults or slashing. Conference notes (AI-generated, so approximate) say TipRouter has distributed over $1 billion of MEV rewards.

What remains in each protocol is mostly its own anchor asset. On 2026-11-06 Jito Restaking TVL was 91.1% JitoSOL, 7.4% JTO, 0.8% KYROS and 0.6% BNSOL. Solayer TVL was 75.9% SOL, 7.2% USDC, 4.6% INF, 3.8% BNSOL, 3.7% JitoSOL, 2.0% mSOL and 1.9% bbSOL. DefiLlama lists JITOSOL under tokensExcludedFromParent for Jito Restaking, which I read as the Jito parent total leaving that JitoSOL out to avoid double counting. Jito Restaking therefore adds almost no new SOL; it re-deposits JitoSOL.

Leaving a Jito vault goes through a non-cancellable cooldown. The withdrawal guide says two epochs (about 4-5 days), with a 0.1% withdrawal fee plus a 0.1% program fee (0.2% total), no rewards once cooldown starts, and the VRT locked in the holder's wallet. The guide also notes that selling the VRT on a secondary market avoids the cooldown at a possible discount. Individual vaults may add their own fees.

A May 2025 Jito Labs talk (AI-generated notes on Solana Compass, which warn they 'may not be 100% accurate') cited over $300M TVL, more than 20 node operators and over a billion dollars of historical MEV distributions through the Tip Router. DefiLlama showed $275M on 2025-05-01 and $334M on 2025-06-01, consistent with the TVL figure; the operator and distribution figures have no second source.

JIP-6 phased the Jito rollout as Deposits (Vault Program, 10 bps withdrawal fee), then Staking (Restaking Program plus a Jito Rewards NCN with a 4% fee on NCN rewards), then Slashing. The current withdrawal guide's 0.1% withdrawal fee matches the 10 bps in JIP-6.

JIP-7 (posted 2024-10-10) proposed a 2,000,000 JTO NCN grants program over two years. Grants of 75,000, 150,000 or 300,000 JTO would be paid in two halves, and the first half would go to a project only if a prediction market rated it at least 50% likely to generate $250K, $500K or $1M of economic value within six months. The proposal said no fully live restaking platform with working NCN staking, slashing and reward payouts existed yet. The fetched page shows no final vote result, and no source read says whether any grant was paid.

An outside user opened issue 281 on 2026-08-13 alleging that operator_set_fee.rs applies an operator fee change immediately. The reporter says an operator could set its fee to 100% just before the Tip Router reward snapshot, let the snapshot capture it, then restore the old fee in the same transaction, which would redirect rewards already earned. On 2026-11-06 the issue is still open. Its only comment is the reporter's follow-up of 2026-08-22 asking why no team response or bounty has come. By DefiLlama's separate listings, two third-party liquid restaking products make up nearly all of Jito Restaking's TVL. Fragmetric ($327.4M) plus Kyros ($35.6M) equal 92% of the $395.9M peak on 2025-07-01, and Fragmetric's fall from $327.4M to $125.8M by 2025-08-01 is about the same size as Jito Restaking's $197M fall that month. Kyros alone was $12.0M, or 76%, of Jito Restaking's $15.8M on 2026-11-05 (9% at the peak). The listings do not reconcile exactly (Fragmetric plus Kyros exceeded the total by $7.3M on 2026-03-01) and the overlap was not checked onchain.

DefiLlama TVL has fallen about 96% for Jito Restaking and 98% for Solayer. Jito Restaking: $395.9M peak on 2025-07-01 (the series starts at its 2025-04-04 listing), $14.8M on 2026-11-06. Solayer: $520.7M peak on 2025-01-23, $9.76M on 2026-11-06. The fall is not a SOL-price effect: JitoSOL held in Jito Restaking dropped from 1.96M tokens to 114K (-94%), and SOL held in Solayer from 1.63M to 82K (-95%), between each peak and 2026-11-05.

Token outflows, not price, explain most of the TVL fall in DefiLlama's own unit series. JitoSOL held in Jito Restaking vaults fell from 1,962,438 units (2025-07-01) to 391,117 (2025-11-06) and 114,255 (2026-11-06), a 94% drop, while the implied JitoSOL price fell 37% ($188.60 to $118.03). Units have been almost flat since 2026-05-10 (116,925). SOL in Solayer fell from 1,629,377 units (2025-01-23) to 301,464 (2025-11-06) and 82,270 (2026-11-06), a 95% drop, while the implied SOL price fell 66% ($264.01 to $90.04). TipRouter is the flagship NCN. The Q2 2026 Blockworks Advisory report (funded by the Jito Foundation) says it collects tips and, since JIP-16, priority fees, and charges 3% on the tips it distributes, split 2.7% to the DAO, 0.15% to JitoSOL stakers and 0.15% to JTO stakers. Kiln gave the same 3% and 2.7/0.15/0.15 split in February 2025.

Jito's own stated success metric is fees, not TVL. In JIP-6 (reply of 2024-11-14) the Foundation wrote that a restaking protocol's success 'should be measured by the amount of economic value that it generates, meaning fees paid to participants from the NCN systems', and called TVL a base of economic security. JIP-6 set a 10 bps vault withdrawal fee and a 4% fee on NCN rewards. Blockworks' Q2 2026 report puts Jito's total protocol revenue at $1.28M and lists no vault or NCN-reward fee line, only TipRouter fees.

DefiLlama TVL for Jito Restaking peaked at about $395.9M on 2025-06-30 (a May 2025 Jito Labs talk cited over $300M and more than 20 operators) and had fallen to about $14.8M by 2026-11-06. Solayer peaked at about $520.7M on 2025-01-22 and stood at about $9.76M on 2026-11-06. The two protocols together hold about $24.6M, under 5% of either peak-era figure. None of the sources read attributes the fall to SOL price, outflows or lost demand.

Fees stack at several levels. Jito's guide lists a 4% protocol reward fee, a 0.1% protocol withdrawal fee, vault-specific deposit, withdrawal and reward fees and operator service fees, and notes 'Vault fees can be updated by admins'. The vault stores four separate fee parameters in basis points, and Certora M-03 found set_reward_fee_bps, set_program_fee_bps and set_withdrawal_fee_bps had no upper-bound check until Jito's fix in PR #184.

Derived estimate, not a reported figure: if the 0.15% + 0.15% shares apply to all Q2 2026 tips ($9.9M per the Blockworks Advisory report), the two restaking-side shares total about $30,000 for the quarter, roughly 0.7% a year on the $16.5M DefiLlama showed for Jito Restaking on 2026-06-01. The estimate assumes the shares go only to restaking-vault depositors, which the two sources word differently.

Solayer's published materials contain no slashing mechanics for sSOL delegated to an endoAVS. The sSOL overview, the Mega Validator and endoAVS page and the delegate-tokens page (gitbook, 'last updated 2 years ago') carry no slashing or risk language, and Binance Research (2025-02-11) makes no slashing statement; its only penalty-related item is 'fraud proof with verifier staking and voting', planned for Solayer Chain in Q3-Q4 2025. This is an absence in the pages read, not proof that no rules exist.

None of the four Solayer documentation pages read (the old GitBook Delegate Tokens page, and the current Delegate Tokens, Mega Validator and endoAVS, and sSOL overview pages) mentions slashing for sSOL delegated to an endoAVS. The risks the docs name are smart-contract risk, Solayer's choice of validators and, for sUSD, issuer risk. Whether any slashing condition exists is unknown.

Jito's user guide lists these restaker risks: slashing due to operator misbehaviour (which 'may or may not be turned on'), custom vault programs, vault admins changing fees, technical risk from new NCNs, NCNs ceasing operations, and liquidity and exit risk when selling a VRT. Kiln (2025-02-27) adds that a VRT may not redeem 1:1, that vault contract or governance flaws could cause loss, and that centralisation could follow if a few NCNs attract most restaked assets.

Slashing interacts badly with vault share maths, which is why the audits pushed it out. OtterSec OS-JRS-ADV-01 (High): if slashing drives a vault's deposited tokens to zero while VRTs stay outstanding, calculate_vrt_mint_amount mints 1:1 and the next depositor effectively donates funds to old VRT holders; repeated slashes also risk overflow. Certora's second report, H-01 (High), found zero-supply states permanently break the VRT:token ratio and warned 'Future slashing mechanisms could trigger this vulnerability'. The audits found five recurring bug classes. (1) Share accounting: a first depositor could inflate the share rate by donating tokens (OtterSec ADV-04, high, PR 150), and zero-supply states broke the VRT-to-token ratio (Certora v2 H-01, PR 150). (2) Slashing dilution: after a full slash, later depositors got too few VRT shares (OtterSec ADV-01, high), resolved by deleting Slash in PR 141. (3) Withdrawal queue: any VRT holder could burn VRT to bypass withdrawal tickets (OtterSec ADV-00, critical, PR 137), and extra VRT sent to the ticket account desynchronized it (ADV-02, PR 140). DefiLlama's protocol API returns three parallel daily arrays: tvl (USD), tokens (units per asset) and tokensInUsd (USD per asset). Dividing tokensInUsd by tokens gives an implied unit price for each asset. Comparing the unit series with the USD series separates real flows from price moves, which a USD-only chart cannot do.

A Jito vault cannot use a Token-2022 mint in practice. Offside Labs rated 'Vault with Token-2022 Mint is Unusable' Low and Jito acknowledged it. Certora's second report flagged inconsistent token-program validation (fixed by PR #175, merged 2024-12-16, which standardises on the original SPL token program), and Jito declined its extension-validation finding because 'Token2022 is no longer supported'. JIP-6 had already said Token-2022 support would not be available initially.

The jito-foundation/restaking repository is Apache-2.0, was created 2024-07-25 and was last pushed 2026-08-11. GitHub lists five releases: v0.0.1 (2024-09-04), v0.0.2 (2024-10-25), v0.0.3 (2024-10-30), v0.0.4 (2025-01-27) and v1.0.0-cli (2025-05-01). The docs list program version 0.0.5, but no 0.0.5 tag exists, so the deployed bytecode cannot be matched to a tagged release. Recent commits are crankers, CLI and keeper work, for example 'Vault Parity' (2026-07-31) and 'CLI: Add cli crate into workspace' (2026-08-11). The repo also ships Rust and TypeScript clients and shank IDLs.

Solayer's design differs from Jito's: a user converts SOL to sSOL, the stake is delegated to Solayer-recommended validators, and the sSOL is then delegated to a Solana dApp (an 'endogenous AVS') that receives AVS wrapper tokens as proof of stake. The dApp gains stake-weighted block-space priority, holders earn Solana staking yield plus MEV yield, and the dApp earns a share of staking commission. Solayer currently chooses the validators; letting dApps choose them is described as a future goal.

Solayer's flow differs from Jito's: a user converts SOL into sSOL (staked with Solayer-recommended validators), then delegates sSOL to a Solana dApp, an 'endogenous AVS', which receives an AVS wrapper token. The dApp gets stake-weighted quality of service (block-space priority) and a share of staking commission; holders earn staking yield plus MEV yield. dApps cannot yet choose the validators, which the docs call a future goal. Binance Research (2025-02-11) says the endogenous AVS launched on mainnet in 2024 Q3 with Bonk, AltLayer, SonicSVM and Hashkey.

Operators receive delegated stake but have no direct control of it, and each vault decides how much stake each operator gets. Rewards accrue to the vault, so the VRT price rises instead of rewards being paid out separately. The NCN's registry entry stores no detailed config: accepted tokens, quorum and slashing conditions live in the NCN's own program. In the TipRouter and the default Template NCN, voting weight is frozen in a snapshot at the start of each consensus cycle, so stake moved mid-cycle cannot change voting power; the docs say other NCNs may define different snapshot mechanisms.

Operators receive delegated stake from vaults but do not control it, and each vault decides how much stake each operator receives. Vault rewards accrue to the vault, so the VRT price rises as rewards build rather than rewards being paid out separately.

Jito and Solayer sell different things. Jito's NCN framework serves arbitrary proof-of-stake services such as oracles, DePINs, bridges, whole chains or reward distribution, and each NCN defines its own consensus, rewards and (in future) slashing. Solayer's endoAVS is a Solana dApp that buys stake-weighted block-space priority with delegated sSOL, and Solayer chooses the validators. A 2024 third-party post drew the same split and called its view of Jito a guess.

Jito targets external, arbitrary proof-of-stake services (NCNs such as oracles, bridges, DePIN and the Tip Router that distributes MEV tips), whereas Solayer's first stage targets applications inside Solana. A third-party 2024 blog framed this split but called its view of Jito 'speculation'.

Skepticism predates both launches. CoinDesk (2024-05-01) quoted Blockworks Research's Ryan Connor saying Solana has 'far less of a need' for restaking than Ethereum because it is 'integrated' rather than 'modular'. At that point Picasso ran Solana's only working restaking product, with about $8M deposited.

Jito's own metric for restaking is fees paid, not TVL: in JIP-6 (2024-11-14) Jito wrote that 'the success of a restaking protocol should be measured by the amount of economic value that it generates, meaning fees paid to participants from the NCN systems'. By that measure, the Q2 2026 Blockworks Advisory report for Jito shows no restaking TVL and no vault revenue line; the only NCN revenue it itemises is TipRouter's, which is Jito's own NCN.

Both programs are upgradeable under Jito DAO governance. JIP-6 placed the protocol and its fee parameters under the DAO, and its thread records that the DAO Security Council started votes on 2025-01-25 to upgrade both programs after a Certora audit. The repo has commits titled 'V2.1 upgrade (#203)' on 2025-02-14 and 'V2.2 upgrade (#250)' on 2025-06-20, so later commits changed the code after the four 2024 audits.

The JitoSOL restaking guide (updated 2025-08-13) names two NCNs as current targets for JitoSOL: TipRouter (Jito's MEV tip and reward distribution protocol) and Switchboard (a decentralised oracle network). Kiln (2025-02-27) named only the Tip Router NCN as live. The guide's prerequisites list SOL, JitoSOL, mSOL and bSOL as supported assets while its NCN section lists JitoSOL only, and the page does not reconcile the two.

Restaking is now one product among several at Solayer. The Solayer docs index lists Solayer Chain, sSOL, sUSD, Solayer Pay and sBridge sections, and DefiLlama groups Solayer, Solayer Restaking, Solayer USD and Solayer Card under one parent. DefiLlama's description still calls Solayer 'the restaking protocol on Solana', while the current Solayer docs call sSOL a liquid staking token.

Jito's own pages still treat slashing as pending. The core docs say 'the slashing functionality is still currently being developed'; the JitoSOL restaking guide warns 'The slashing feature may or may not be turned on. Check before you deposit'; the 2024 Immunefi scope said slashing would not be enabled at launch 'as an initial guardrail'; JIP-6 made slashing a third phase and says slashing on any NCN needs node-operator and VRT approval before activation, and Jito edited that timeline on 2024-11-14 'as development timelines have evolved'. A May 2025 Jito Labs talk still listed slashing as plan

Jito targets external proof-of-stake services as NCNs (oracles, bridges, DePIN, MEV tip distribution), while Solayer's first stage targeted applications inside Solana, which its docs call endogenous AVSs; exogenous AVSs such as oracles and bridges are the other category. A 2024 Substack analysis drew this line but called its read of Jito's focus speculation (the post is in Chinese).

Jito's restaking contracts had three independent 2024 audits (OtterSec 2024-10-25, Certora, Offside Labs), plus a $150,000 Immunefi audit competition from 2024-11-04 to 2024-12-02 over about 14,000 lines in four programs. Certora's second report found 10 issues (5 high, 3 medium, 2 low), including zero-supply states that break VRT ratios, incorrect asset unstaking and inconsistent token validation.

Jito ran a $150,000 audit competition on Immunefi from 2024-11-04 to 2024-12-02 (rewards in JTO; about 14,000 lines; Restaking Core, Restaking Program, Vault Core and Vault Program in scope). It listed three known issues as ineligible: first-depositor share-rate inflation by donating to a vault (PR #150), fee changes between withdrawal enqueue and burn (unresolved then), and an oversized cooldown reserve after a missed vault update (PR #163). GitHub shows PR #150 and PR #163 both merged on 2024-12-23.

Jito restaking slashing was not live in the documentation last updated 2025-08-13. The audit competition excluded slashing at launch 'as an initial guardrail', JIP-6 put slashing in a later phase that needs NCN, node-operator and VRT approval, and a May 2025 Jito Labs talk listed slashing as a planned feature. No source found confirms slashing has shipped since.

Solayer's docs describe a 3-of-5 multisig for upgrades of the Solayer program (ID sSo1iU21jBrU9VaJ8PJib1MtorefUV4fzC9GURa2KNn): community seats held by Bison Trails, Marinade and OtterSec's Robert Chen, a core-team seat, and a fifth community seat not yet filled. No timelock is mentioned and the page is undated.

Solayer's restaking program (sSo1iU21jBrU9VaJ8PJib1MtorefUV4fzC9GURa2KNn) was last deployed 2024-09-05. Its upgrade authority is GcYvLKKEWpxQMqFe9HUcDJYMGvXt7kwf8gfBvjnW4wnm, the same address the Solayer docs name as a 3-of-5 multisig. The docs list seat holders from Bison Trail, Marinade Finance and OtterSec plus two Solayer core-team keys. The docs page is undated, so the current seat holders are unverified.

A secondary source reports that Solayer is sunsetting sUSD. MadeOnSol (published 2026-05-17, updated 2026-11-04) says the Solayer announcements channel gives these dates: deposits close August 1, yield ends September 30, self-service withdrawals end December 31, with manual handling afterwards. The page states no year and asserts no sUSD TVL. It also says Solayer's documentation as of November 2026 still describes sUSD as a yield-bearing stablecoin, and the docs index still lists sUSD pages. No official Solayer notice was found.

DefiLlama's Jito Restaking TVL was $219.8M on 2025-04-04 (series start), $349.4M on 2025-05-20, a peak of $395.9M on 2025-07-01, $203.0M on 2025-08-13, $156.0M on 2025-09-30, $38.1M on 2025-12-31, $16.0M on 2026-03-31, $15.5M on 2026-06-30, $20.1M on 2026-09-30 and $14.8M on 2026-11-06. Solayer lists audits of its restaking program, endoAVS and sUSD by OtterSec (April and July 2024) and Halborn (August to October 2024). The Halborn report page I fetched rendered no findings, so severities and remediation are unverified.
Jito's restaking repository is Apache-2.0, shows no published releases and 3 open issues, and the docs list program version 0.0.5.

Solayer lists five audits, all dated 2024: OtterSec (token metadata in April, restaking program in July) and Halborn (endoAVS and a pool/restaking program in August, sUSD in October). OtterSec's restaking report (assessed 2024-04-22 to 04-25, follow-up 2024-07-24, commit ad83447) found 3 issues: a High where the freeze-account check read the wrong account, a centralisation note about a non-zero initial RST supply, and a validation suggestion. That code uses the earlier RST-token naming. The Halborn PDFs are image-only and could not be read; Halborn's page advises a follow-up within six months

Jito's four public audit reports all date from 2024. Certora v1 (2024-08-08 to 2024-09-19) found 22 issues: 0 critical, 4 high, 7 medium, 6 low and 5 informational, with 18 fixed. OtterSec (assessed 2024-09-20 to 2024-10-10, report dated 2024-10-25, commit f04242f) found 8 issues: 1 critical, 4 high and 3 informational, and marked all five vulnerabilities resolved. Offside Labs (2024-10-28 to 2024-11-06, commit 60b3884) found 6 issues: 1 medium (fixed), 1 low and 4 informational. Solayer's docs list five audits: OtterSec in April 2024 (token metadata) and July 2024 (restaking program), and Halborn in August 2024 (endoAVS), August 2024 (pool) and October 2024 (sUSD). The page promises 'two audits per year on all existing contracts' but lists none after October 2024. The Halborn report page rendered no findings, so severities and fixes are unverified.

Immunefi's post of 2024-09-06 announced a Jito Foundation bug bounty with up to $250,000 for critical issues and $100,000 for high issues, paid in JTO. Its listed scope was Jito-Solana, Jito-Relayer, Jito Programs and Stakenet, with no restaking programs. A search snippet said restaking-core was added on 2025-01-21, but the Immunefi scope page returned 404, so current bounty coverage of the restaking programs is unconfirmed.

No exploit of either protocol was found. DefiLlama's hacks array is empty for both Jito Restaking and Solayer on 2026-11-06, and a targeted web search for exploits of either returned none. The only open security item found is the third-party issue 281 in the Jito repository, which is unreviewed.
